ctx.x: ever opened in Barcelona. I remember that the pianist was called Sandy but I never learned his real Spanish name. All of the musicians were Spanish and they were not too bad at playing jazz, considering that there were very very few places where jazz had ever been played in this country and therefore the musicians there, that went for jazz, had very few occasions to play and experiment with the kind of music they enjoyed.

There were two tenor men in the group I worked with. One was known as Pocholo who also played clarinet and was very popular with the jazz fans. The other tenor man was Salvador Font whom I had jammed with in Rome way back in 1950. The jazz fans in Barcelona were mostly the rich people because they were the ones that could afford to buy jazz records and there was quite a large number of them. In June I was contacted to play at the "Vieux Colombier" in Juan-les-Pins, the club that Sydney Bechet made famous some year before. Badel, the owner, who also owned the Juan for the month of July and August. He was a slick guy and it was very hard to get a decent salary from him.
